exam: 2026年6月 第3套 · 仔细阅读 P1
title: Disgust is a universal human emotion.…

sents.en: Disgust is a universal human emotion.
sents.cn: 厌恶是一种普遍的人类情感。

sents.en: One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects.
sents.cn: 其中一种称为身体厌恶，它保护我们不去吃或触摸可能对我们有危险的东西，比如生肉或昆虫。

sents.en: Children experience physical disgust from a very early age, but do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old.
sents.cn: 儿童从很小的时候就会体验到身体厌恶，但要到大约四岁才真正理解这一概念。

sents.en: Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong.
sents.cn: 一些研究者主张还存在另一种厌恶，称为道德厌恶，它防止我们参与那些被视为道德错误的行为。

sents.en: Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.
sents.cn: 道德厌恶的例子有偷窃、说谎或欺骗。

sents.en: However, not all academics think that moral disgust really exists.
sents.cn: 然而，并非所有学者都认为道德厌恶真的存在。

sents.en: Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor (隐喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.
sents.cn: 有些人说，当我们在道德问题中提及厌恶时，是把厌恶当作一种隐喻（隐喻），而我们实际感受到的是愤怒。

sents.en: If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it.
sents.cn: 如果道德厌恶在发展中相当晚才出现，那么认为它实际上包含社会成分就说得通了。

sents.en: Children learn about emotions in many different ways.
sents.cn: 儿童以许多不同的方式学习情绪。

sents.en: Of special relevance are parents-children conversations about emotions.
sents.cn: 尤其相关的，是父母与子女之间关于情绪的对话。

sents.en: Indeed, children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.
sents.cn: 的确，那些父母常谈论情绪的孩子，往往比父母不常讨论情绪的孩子有更好的情绪理解力。

sents.en: However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust.
sents.cn: 然而，目前还没有研究考察父母与子女是如何谈论厌恶的。

sents.en: This is what we set up to examine in our study.
sents.cn: 这正是我们在研究中着手考察的内容。

sents.en: We asked 68 English-speaking mothers and their four-, six- or eight-year-old children to discuss some stories about moral and physical disgust.
sents.cn: 我们邀请了68位讲英语的母亲及其四岁、六岁或八岁的孩子，讨论一些关于道德与身体厌恶的故事。

sents.en: Our preliminary findings show mothers and children do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.
sents.cn: 我们的初步发现显示，母亲和孩子的确会谈论厌恶，但主要是身体厌恶，而非道德厌恶。

sents.en: When we asked mothers and children to discuss moral issues, such as whether it is OK to play with a child who has stolen someone else's snack, they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.
sents.cn: 当我们请母亲和孩子们讨论道德问题，比如和偷了别人零食的孩子一起玩是否合适时，他们将这类道德过错与愤怒的情绪而非厌恶联系起来。

sents.en: Does this mean that moral disgust does not exist?
sents.cn: 这是否意味着道德厌恶不存在？

sents.en: Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults.
sents.cn: 一些研究者认为道德厌恶存在于成年人中。

sents.en: Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years.
sents.cn: 我们的发现表明，道德厌恶要么是在更大年龄才被理解，要么——即便有——在八岁这么大的孩子中也只是被比喻性地使用。
